stem:
Two characteristics of quadratic function p are given.

• The axis of symmetry of the graph of p is x = -3.
• Function p has exactly one zero.

Based on this information, which graph could represent p?
visual_elements: Graph A: Parabola with vertex at (approximately) (-3, 1) opening downward and crossing x-axis once at x=-3
Graph B: Parabola with vertex at (approximately) (-4.5, 3) opening downward and crossing x-axis twice
Graph C: Parabola with vertex at (approximately) (3, 3) opening downward and crossing x-axis twice
Graph D: Parabola with vertex at (approximately) (3, 1) opening downward and crossing x-axis twice
notes: Answer choices have no text, only labeled graphs. The question is about understanding quadratic properties involving axis of symmetry and number of zeros.
